date_note: Kukmin Ilbo (23 November) says the Seoul education office learned of the leak on 20 November, the survey's last day; the exposure ran during the survey from 3 November.
exec: A Seoul public library survey page exposed participants' names and phone numbers; the education office has blocked access and reported it to regulators.
geo_basis: victim; the library in Jongno-gu, Seoul, as the source states
org: Jeongdok Library (Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education)
plain: Names and phone numbers of 636 people who took a Seoul library's website survey leaked, the city's education office told Kukmin Ilbo. It has stopped the data being viewed and is investigating whether it was hacking.
summary: According to the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, quoted by Kukmin Ilbo, names and mobile numbers of 636 people (936 including duplicates) who took Jeongdok Library's 3-20 November website survey leaked from its gift-voucher page. An official said the data was viewed by manipulating the integrated library site's screen code; whether it was hacking is under investigation. The office says it reported the leak and blocked access.
title: Seoul's Jeongdok Library survey leaks names and phone numbers of 636 people

validation.note: One publisher read (Kukmin Ilbo, exclusive, quoting the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education and its 23 November notice to users); searches found no second report or the office's own notice page.

evidence.quote: 교육청에 따르면 유출된 항목은 설문조사에 참여한 636명(중복 포함 936명)의 이름과 휴대전화번호다.
교육청은 설문조사 마지막 날인 지난 20일 개인정보 유출 사실을 인지했고 즉시 교육부과 개인정보보호위원회에 신고했다.
